bib.title: True Few-Shot Learning with Language Models

question: How well do few-shot LMs perform when prompts and hyperparameters must be chosen using only the few training examples, with no held-out validation set?
hypothesis: Prior few-shot results overestimate LM ability because prompts and hyperparameters were tuned on many held-out examples; true few-shot selection will do much worse.
contributions: Disambiguate three few-shot settings: multi-distribution, tuned, and true few-shot learning
Evaluate cross-validation and minimum description length for prompt selection on 9 LMs and hyperparameter selection for ADAPET
Recommendations for reporting true few-shot learning

method.summary: Candidate prompts (LAMA, RTE, CB, WiC) or hyperparameters (ADAPET on SuperGLUE) are scored with leave-one-out CV or MDL online coding using only N training examples, and the test accuracy of the selected option is compared with the worst, mean (random) and best (held-out-selected) option.
method.task: model selection (prompt and hyperparameter choice) for few-shot learning

datasets.name: LAMA TREx (LAMA-UHN subset)
datasets.split: N=5 training examples per relation (also 10,15,20,30,40); test = one example per permutation, 120 for N=5, excluding training examples
datasets.source: Petroni et al. 2019; UHN filter Poerner et al. 2020; CC 4.0
datasets.preprocessing: Answer is top-predicted token out of 20k candidates; 5 runs with different training sets

datasets.name: RTE, CB, WiC
datasets.size: full validation set for held-out accuracy
datasets.split: 5 training examples sampled from task train set with at least one per class; 5 train sets

datasets.name: SuperGLUE (BoolQ, CB, COPA, RTE, WiC, WSC, MultiRC, ReCoRD)
datasets.split: FewGLUE 32-example subset plus 3 random 32-example subsets (four train sets); validation set for eval
datasets.source: Wang et al. 2019; FewGLUE Schick and Schutze
datasets.preprocessing: first ADAPET prompt used for every task

other.note: inferred sizes: assumed the four largest in Brown et al. since OpenAI does not disclose API model sizes

models.name: ADAPET
models.architecture: ALBERT-xxlarge-v2 finetuned with label-discrimination and masked-LM objectives

training.objective: ADAPET: classify each label as correct or incorrect given input, plus predict randomly masked input tokens given label (GPT models: no training, in-context only)
training.steps: T = 1000 gradient updates; checkpoint chosen from {250, 500, 750, 1000}
training.hardware: single AMD MI50 GPU (32GB) for up to 12 hours per model and hyperparameter setting
training.compute: GPT-3 API cost $2826.73 total; GPT-2 experiments at most 8 hours on one MI50
training.wall_clock: up to 12 hours per ADAPET setting
training.seeds: 4 train sets (FewGLUE + 3 random 32-example subsets) for ADAPET; 5 train sets for prompt experiments

other.cv_mdl_folds_adapet: K = 8 folds; MDL uses 16 examples in the first fold and 2 per fold for 8 more; first fold scored with uniform distribution
other.final_model: retrained on full dataset with chosen T and M

inference.decoding: in-context completion; class probabilities by softmax over label-name logits
inference.samples: 5 runs with different training sets; expectation over N! = 120 example orders (N=5) or 120 sampled permutations (N>=10)
inference.prompting: 5-shot (LAMA, RTE, CB, WiC); up to 16 candidate prompts per LAMA relation (mean 12); 3 prompts RTE/CB, 4 prompts WiC

parameters.cv: leave-one-out (K = N) for prompt experiments; K=8 for ADAPET
parameters.loss: negative log-likelihood of label given input
parameters.conservative_alpha: alpha in {1,2,3} for CV_alpha, tested on GPT-3 175B only

metrics.name: LAMA accuracy
metrics.definition: top-predicted token (of 20k candidates) matches a true answer

metrics.name: Relative test accuracy of chosen prompt
metrics.definition: average prompt scaled to 0, best prompt scaled to 100

metrics.name: Accuracy at choosing top prompt
metrics.definition: how often the criterion picks the prompt with highest test accuracy

metrics.name: SuperGLUE per-task metrics
metrics.definition: Acc, Acc/F1, EM/F1 as per task; Avg over tasks

baselines: best chosen with held-out accuracy (prior work)
ADAPET, iPET, PET, GPT-3 published SuperGLUE numbers
eval.protocol: mean and std. err. over 5 train sets (prompt experiments) or mean std dev over four 32-shot train sets (ADAPET); no significance test stated

prompts.text:
His family has steadfastly denied the charges.
question: The charges were denied by his family. True or False?
answer: True  (labels: True, False)

The charges were denied by his family?
His family has steadfastly denied the charges.
Therefore, the answer is yes.  (labels: yes, no)

"The charges were denied by his family"?
"His family has steadfastly denied the charges.", so the answer is yes.  (labels: yes, no)

Room and board.
He nailed boards across the windows.
question: Is the word 'board' used in the same way in the two sentences above?
answer: no  (labels: no, yes)
CB and WiC prompts 2-3 (and WiC prompt 4 with sense labels 2a, 1b) follow Schick and Schutze templates; see Table 2 for full text

results.claim: CV and MDL prompt selection underperform the best held-out-selected prompt by 5-7% absolute on LAMA-UHN on average.
results.quote: Prompts chosen by CV and MDL alike underperform the best prompt (chosen using held-out performance) by 5-7% absolute on average.

results.claim: CV/MDL close only 20-40% of the gap between average and best prompts.
results.quote: but only close the gap between the average and best prompts by 20-40%, as shown in Fig. 1 (right).

results.claim: For GPT-3 175B, CV picks the best prompt only 21% of the time vs 9% for chance.
results.quote: only 21% accuracy for CV vs. 9% for random chance

results.claim: For models 0.1B-6.7B the chance CV-chosen prompt beats the average prompt is only about 56% (MDL about 55%).
results.quote: the chance of improving over the average, randomly-chosen prompt is only ∼56% for CV and ∼55% for MDL

results.claim: There is about a 27% chance selection causes an accuracy drop of about 13%.
results.setup: LAMA-UHN, all model sizes, CV and MDL
results.quote: there is a ∼27% chance that prompt selection causes an accuracy drop of ∼13% for all model sizes and CV/MDL alike

results.claim: For GPT-3 175B, selected prompts are 40% worse than average 5% of the time.
Conservative CV_alpha does not help: CV beats the average prompt 50% of the time vs 51% for alpha=2.
results.quote: CV outperforms the average prompt 50% of the time vs. 51% for α = 2

results.claim: Raising N from 5 to 40 examples gives no consistent improvement in prompt selection.
results.setup: LAMA, models up to 6.7B, N in {5,10,15,20,30,40}
results.quote: Even in higher-data regimes (40 examples), CV/MDL struggle to choose effective prompts

results.claim: More compute does not help: accuracy plateaus after 1 forward pass for MDL and N for CV.
results.quote: test accuracy roughly plateaus after one forward pass for MDL and N forward passes for CV

results.claim: CV gives a 20% chance of a 15% accuracy drop on CB for GPT-3 175B.
results.quote: For CB, there is a 20% change of a 15% accuracy drop for GPT-3 175B.

results.claim: True few-shot hyperparameter selection drops ADAPET by 2-10% across 8 tasks.
results.quote: true few-shot selection causes performance to drop by 2-10% across 8 tasks for ADAPET [12]

results.claim: ADAPET SuperGLUE average with CV-chosen hyperparameters is 73.0 (MDL 73.4) vs mean 73.9 and best 77.2.
results.setup: ADAPET, SuperGLUE validation, four 32-shot train sets, 16 hyperparameter combinations
results.note: Other rows: MDL 73.4, Mean 73.9, Best 77.2, Worst 69.4, ADAPET 77.3, iPET 76.8, PET 74.1, GPT-3 73.2

results.claim: In the true few-shot setting ADAPET's average falls below PET/iPET.
results.setup: as above; CV 73.0 and MDL 73.4 vs iPET 76.8
results.quote: the average SuperGLUE performance of ADAPET drops below that of earlier methods (PET and iPET)
results.note: iPET 76.8 and PET 74.1 are reported numbers from Schick and Schutze in Table 1

results.claim: CV needs more than 2-3k examples to pick better-than-average ADAPET hyperparameters on WiC and MultiRC.
results.quote: CV requires >2-3k examples to choose better-than-average hyperparameters

results.claim: Other criteria (Bayesian CV, MDL_beta, joint log-prob) also choose prompts near the random average.
results.quote: all criteria choose prompts with a similar average accuracy, close to the average accuracy of randomly-chosen prompts

results.claim: GPT-3 experiments cost $2826.73 via the OpenAI API.
results.quote: costing a total of $2826.73 for all experiments

limits: Study not exhaustive; other criteria or heuristics might work (Sec 6)
Prompt experiments on LAMA and 3 classification tasks with GPT-family models up to 175B; N up to 40 because of the 2048-token context
GPT-3 sizes assumed (not disclosed by OpenAI)
Effects of selection with thousands of examples only preliminary (Appendix C)
Full-results Fig 6 task numbers read from plots only
Uses LM era of 2021 (GPT-3, GPT-2); instruction-tuned models not tested
